evidence.excerpt:
YOLOv7 surpasses all known object detectors in both
speed and accuracy in the range from 5 FPS to 160 FPS
and has the highest accuracy 56.8% AP among all known
real-time object detectors with 30 FPS or higher on GPU
V100. YOLOv7-E6 object detector (56 FPS V100, 55.9%
AP) outperforms both transformer-based detector SWIN-
L Cascade-Mask R-CNN (9.2 FPS A100, 53.9% AP) by
509% in speed and 2% in accuracy, and convolutional-
based detector ConvNeXt-XL Cascade-Mask R-CNN (8.6
FPS A100, 55.2% AP) by 551% in speed and 0.7% AP
in accuracy, as well as YOLOv7 outperforms: YOLOR,
YOLOX, Scaled-YOLOv4, YOLOv5, DETR, Deformable
DETR, DINO-5scale-R50, ViT-Adapter-B and many other
object detectors in speed and accuracy. Moreover, we train
YOLOv7 only on MS COCO dataset from scratch without
using any other datasets or pre-trained weights. Source
code is released in https://github.com/WongKinYiu/yolov7.

lows: (1) we design several trainable bag-of-freebies meth-
ods, so that real-time object detection can greatly improve
the detection accuracy without increasing the inference
cost; (2) for the evolution of object detection methods, we
found two new issues, namely how re-parameterized mod-
ule replaces original module, and how dynamic label as-
signment strategy deals with assignment to different output
layers. In addition, we also propose methods to address the
difficulties arising from these issues; (3) we propose "ex-
tend" and "compound scaling" methods for the real-time
object detector that can effectively utilize parameters and
computation; and (4) the method we proposed can effec-
tively reduce about 40% parameters and 50% computation
of state-of-the-art real-time object detector, and has faster
inference speed and higher detection accuracy.

inferred from the above phenomenon that
we cannot analyze different scaling factors separately for
a concatenation-based model but must be considered to-
gether. Take scaling-up depth as an example, such an ac-
tion will cause a ratio change between the input channel and
output channel of a transition layer, which may lead to a de-
crease in the hardware usage of the model. Therefore, we
must propose the corresponding compound model scaling
method for a concatenation-based model. When we scale
the depth factor of a computational block, we must also cal-
culate the change of the output channel of that block. Then,
we will perform width factor scaling with the same amount
of change on the transition layers, and the result is shown
in Figure 3 (c). Our proposed compound scaling method
can maintain the properties that the model had at the initial
design and maintains the optimal structure.

and validate our object detection method. All our experi-
ments did not use pre-trained models. That is, all models
were trained from scratch. During the development pro-
cess, we used train 2017 set for training, and then used val
2017 set for verification and choosing hyperparameters. Fi-
nally, we show the performance of object detection on the
test 2017 set and compare it with the state-of-the-art object
detection algorithms. Detailed training parameter settings
are described in Appendix.
We designed basic model for edge GPU, normal GPU,
and cloud GPU, and they are respectively called YOLOv7-
tiny, YOLOv7, and YOLOv7-W6. At the same time, we
also use basic model for model scaling for different ser-
vice requirements and get different types of models. For
YOLOv7, we do stack scaling on neck, and use the pro-
posed compound scaling

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported gains are corroborated by standard COCO val and test-dev AP measurements, which are external to the lead-head-guided label assignment used during training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported as standard MS COCO AP metrics on val and test-dev sets against held-out ground-truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system is trained with supervised classification, regression, and objectness losses, with soft labels generated by the lead head's own predictions guiding both auxiliary and lead heads.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics (e.g., reaching up to 56.8% AP on MS COCO test-dev/val at real-time speeds) directly support the claim of advancing state-of-the-art Pareto frontiers in accuracy and inference speed without pre-trained backbones.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is conducted systematically on the standard MS COCO benchmark from scratch, comparing comprehensively against contemporary real-time detectors (PP-YOLOE, YOLOR, YOLOX, YOLOv5) across parameter counts, FLOPs, and FPS on standard hardware. Extensive ablation studies validate the specific contributions of compound scaling, planned RepConv, and auxiliary label guidance.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline gains are corroborated by standard COCO val and test-dev AP benchmarks, run independently of the internal lead-guided label assigner.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard Microsoft COCO average precision (AP) metrics evaluated against held-out ground truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard multi-task loss optimization (classification, regression, objectness) using supervised ground truth and soft labels guided by the lead head.

primary.limitations: The manuscript focuses almost exclusively on MS COCO and GPU architectures, providing limited discussion on cross-domain generalization, specialized hardware quantization behavior, or theoretical boundaries of the multi-head auxiliary loss weighting.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly articulated, providing structural rationale for gradient path preservation in E-ELAN, mathematically motivated compound scaling across depth and width, re-parameterization adjustments to avoid breaking residual/concatenation flows, and hierarchical soft-label assignment between auxiliary and lead heads.
primary.quality_rationale: YOLOv7 provides a well-engineered, thoroughly benchmarked real-time detection family with clear ablations on all claimed architectural and optimization components. The evaluation uses standard objective benchmarks and standardized measurement protocols.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces YOLOv7, a real-time object detection framework incorporating extended efficient layer aggregation networks (E-ELAN), compound model scaling for concatenation-based architectures, planned re-parameterized convolution, and a coarse-to-fine lead-head guided dynamic label assignment strategy.

scholarly_quality.rationale: YOLOv7 provides a well-engineered, thoroughly benchmarked real-time detection family with clear ablations on all claimed architectural and optimization components. The evaluation uses standard objective benchmarks and standardized measurement protocols.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript focuses almost exclusively on MS COCO and GPU architectures, providing limited discussion on cross-domain generalization, specialized hardware quantization behavior, or theoretical boundaries of the multi-head auxiliary loss weighting.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
